Could it be… that the two selectable greens are actually one "domino" object (two connected green blocks)? No, they were separate N nodes (12px each).

Oh, wait. I think I get it! The two selectable greens are "screws" that get removed when you click their border target, and the new green at (18,29) is… hmm, no.

Let me look at the image again: the top row has two adjacent greens at (18,29) and (18,35)?? No wait — the segmentation says N is at (18,29) and (18,35). In the image they look adjacent (columns 29-32 and 35-38, with 33-34 between them — a 2px gap, which looks nearly adjacent at this scale).
So current state: green at (18,29), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41).
Compared to the initial state: (18,17), (18,23), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41).
Net: (18,17) and (18,23) → (18,29).
Hmm, what if the mechanic is "merge": select a green, click the target, and the selected green and its adjacent green (in the direction of the target?) merge into one at the target position? (18,17) is selected, target (18,29) is to the right; the green to the right of (18,17) is (18,23); both merge at (18,29)?
Or more simply: the game is "2048-style merging" or "block pushing."
